Sorry for the delay. Changes in the latest commit:
1. change the route to align with GitHub: `workflows/{workflow_name}/badge.svg` with `event` and `branch` para
2. use `.Badge` instead of `$`
3. hardcoded background color and shadow instead of calculating luminance
4. add content header `image/svg+xml`
5. simply code

From my test, badges are still the same as in this PR's description.

How performant are the `drawer.MeasureString` calls? GitHub and shields.io use pre calculated character width tables to prevent such measuring (https://github.com/metabolize/anafanafo/tree/main/packages/anafanafo).

If we want to use badges for other stuff too I would make sense to move the bade generation code to a new module `code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/badge`.

> How performant are the `drawer.MeasureString` calls? GitHub and shields.io use pre calculated character width tables to prevent such measuring (https://github.com/metabolize/anafanafo/tree/main/packages/anafanafo).

Interesting module. So it uses around 250kB of JSON data per font/size combination and has a bit of wrapper code around to do the magic. Shouldn't be too hard to port to go.
Yes, we could just have a helper script which translates that JSON to a GO array and replicate the calculation logic.

> If we want to use badges for other stuff too it would make sense to move the bade generation code to a new module code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/badge.

done

> Needs some docs

done

> How performant are the drawer.MeasureString calls?

I think it's okay. I'm not the font expert here but when I checked the `MesaureString` function, the function basically just checked every char and then advanced. Since the code only uses the basic font `Face7x13`, the advanced rule is pretty simple.
```
func MeasureString(f Face, s string) (advance fixed.Int26_6) {
  prevC := rune(-1)
  for _, c := range s {
    if prevC >= 0 {
      advance += f.Kern(prevC, c)  // it's always 0 in Face7x13
    }
    a, _ := f.GlyphAdvance(c) // for unicode from `\u0080` ~ `\ufffc`, they are same in Face7x13
    advance += a
    prevC = c
  }
  return advance
} 
```

I can accept the idea of creating a map to pre-calculate the Unicode width. But I think this way is more convenient (for me of course 😄 )
Maybe instead of doing precalculation for fonts it would be more efficient to cache generated type|status SVG images?

> Maybe instead of doing precalculation for fonts it would be more efficient to cache generated type|status SVG images?

issue_context.title: Add badge for Gitea Actions to display result in README.md
issue_context.body:
### Feature Description

Like it exists on GitHub or other CI, it could be interesting to add a SVG badge to integrate into markdown in example.

The documentation to use it on GitHub could be found https://docs.github.com/en/actions/monitoring-and-troubleshooting-workflows/adding-a-workflow-status-badge

An URL like `https://<GITEA_INSTANCE>/<OWNER>/<REPOSITORY>/actions/workflows/<WORKFLOW_FILE>/badge.svg` with:
* `GITEA_INSTANCE` the domain/url of the Gate server
* `OWNER` the project owner/organisation
* `REPOSITORY` the repository name
* `WORLFLOW_FILE` the filename of the action that trigged the build, and so, the result of the build

### Screenshots

_No response_
comments:
FWIW, I wrote a small bridge that does something like this: https://git.madhouse-project.org/algernon/ironforge/ (the README in there uses the service for the CI badge).

It's a separate server, and isn't as flexible as proposed here. It just looks at the most recent status, and redirects to an appropriate shields.io URL. It can't filter by workflow (the Gitea APIs don't provide that info yet), but it's close enough, and better than nothing.
